title: Search order: organise by mechanism, not by position (P1 to P17, November 9 to 17, 2026)
scope: Seventeen small preregistered steps on the older Gen2 swarm's search order, plus one read of recorded Gen3 outcomes. Aggregate counts and ratios only. The swarm's original sweep method, the recorded mission data and the mission's name stay private; mechanisms are anonymised.
generation: Gen2 work (the legacy swarm); its lesson is carried forward to Gen3

evidence_labels.scripted: measured on fixtures, no quantum-computer time: scripted test targets with a known answer, scored by code; no model, no real target
evidence_labels.measured_on_ibm_hardware: one run on a real IBM device (P7), billed seconds from IBM's usage record
evidence_labels.measured_recorded: a read of recorded Gen3 outcomes (P14 not blind; the P15 replay blind)

lesson: Organise search by mechanism (the kind of attack), not by where a candidate sits in a list.
independent_lines: the Nano lockpick's scripted-reader result (L0), which searches by the features of a stuck state
recorded Gen3 outcomes, where the mechanism predicts 111 of 125 recorded checks

steps.label: scripted
steps.question: does the swarm's original sweep order home in on the good areas of a test field?
steps.result: no: its final focus zone held fewer good items than random at every size; narrowing's zone also fell short (1 of 3 sizes)

steps.label: scripted
steps.question: narrowing against random order where good items sit together
steps.result: narrowing found 15.9, 15.4 and 14.9 times as many good items as random order at three sizes; the original order 3.6 to 4.8 times

steps.label: scripted
steps.question: the same on messier fields (off-grid, jittered)
steps.result: 13.5 to 14.5 times random on the messiest fields; 18.7 to 20.6 on aligned ones

steps.label: scripted
steps.question: fields built from banked Gen3 task evidence (80 tasks)
steps.result: 7.5, 4.5 and 9.6 times random at drive lengths 6, 7 and 8 (above the line at 6 and 8)

steps.label: scripted
steps.question: 200 fresh tasks, with read noise and dropouts
steps.result: 10.2 and 9.4 times random clean; 8.5 to 10.1 with noise; 7.9 to 8.7 with dropouts

steps.label: scripted
steps.question: narrowing as a hint inside a scripted solver: fewer solver steps?
steps.result: no: 1.10 and 1.06 against the solver's own search, and the hint cost more to make than it saved

steps.label: measured_on_ibm_hardware
steps.question: narrowing on IBM hardware: good candidates per billed second against random order
steps.result: 1.7 and 3.4 times as many good candidates per billed second as random order, at two sizes; 27.0 billed seconds over six jobs; 85 percent of probe indices delivered exactly (one unstable qubit)

steps.label: scripted
steps.question: a hardware repeat with a bad-qubit screen
steps.result: the offline gate passed; the live repeat was never released or run
steps.verdict: offline gate MET; live cells NOT RUN

steps.label: scripted
steps.question: does aligning the sweep make it a solver?
steps.result: no: 0.48 and 0.24 of tasks solved against a 0.50 line

steps.label: built
steps.question: wire narrowing into the swarm behind a setting
steps.result: built; off by default at the time

steps.label: built
steps.question: a Gen3 probe-mission driver that can use narrowing
steps.result: built and tested; nothing calls it yet

steps.label: scripted
steps.question: inside the real swarm loop: narrowing against the original order
steps.result: 6.6 times as many good items; the original order only ever moved on when its time ran out (200 of 200 sessions) and in 9 of 200 sessions sent 3 of 5 agents past the end of the list

steps.label: scripted
steps.question: on the swarm's real list order, with outcomes driven by technique
steps.result: no difference from the original order (0.95) and below no sweep at all (0.77): the list spreads each technique's variants evenly through its category, so position carries little; narrowing became the default under the preregistered rule

steps.label: measured_recorded
steps.question: what decides success in recorded Gen3 outcomes?
steps.result: the mechanism: it predicts 111 of 125 recorded checks (permutation p 0.00001); the best 3 of 17 mechanisms hold 65 percent of the hits on 34 percent of the checks; a technique-grouped list won big on some targets and lost on most, so it was not shipped

steps.label: scripted
steps.question: try every technique once, then focus
steps.result: 200 of 200 test targets reached against 68 percent with no sweep, and 5.4 times the hits; narrowing by position did worse than no sweep
steps.verdict: MET; shipped as the swarm default

steps.label: scripted
steps.question: how much to explore against how much to dig
steps.result: exploring 90 percent of the time found the most mechanisms per target: 0.660 against 0.600 for pure exploring and 0.392 for pure digging; the old setting explored 15 percent

steps.label: scripted
steps.question: does 90/10 hold when the share of working variants changes?
steps.result: yes: within 0.012 of the best at every share from 5 to 100 percent

recorded_outcomes.label: measured_recorded
recorded_outcomes.source: one Gen3 private security mission; local reproductions; no live target; mechanisms anonymised as M01 to M17
recorded_outcomes.caveat: the counts were seen before the preregistration, and promising mechanisms were tested more often

blind_replay_p15.what: the same recorded verdicts read in two orders (reported, not gated)
blind_replay_p15.reading: trying every mechanism in turn reaches almost twice as many mechanisms early; the mission's own order finds more hits early because it kept digging where it had already found something

explore_ratio_p16_p17.label: scripted
explore_ratio_p16_p17.caveat: the test targets use invented numbers (open techniques per target, share of working variants); P17 varied the working share

hardware_p7.label: measured_on_ibm_hardware
hardware_p7.route: direct IBM runtime from a laptop, not Predator's production route
hardware_p7.limits: one run, one device, one calibration window, no repeat; scripted fields; no solver gain; no quantum advantage

shipped.where: draft pull request #489 in the private repository, into a feature branch, not main
defaults: the swarm's list is grouped by technique
the swarm tries every technique once, then focuses
the swarm explores 90 percent of the time (was 15 percent)
shipped.switch_back: each change is one setting away from the old behaviour

kept_private_for_the_loop: a held-out set of 17 recorded mechanisms, to score a future Model 1 choice of which mechanism to test next
879 recorded narrowing decisions that could become replayable steps in Atlas
what_it_does_not_do: it is Gen2 work on the legacy swarm
the test targets were scripted: no real judge and no real target
nothing was replayed or trained into Model 1
it does not touch the Gen4 test (each Model 1 generation reaching further with fewer outside rescues)
still_open: a smaller swarm defect wastes about 3 percent of turns (2.7 percent) when a focus zone is smaller than the number of agents
the live hardware repeat (P8) was never run
the Gen3 probe-mission driver (P11) has no caller
proposed_next: Not started: bring the rule (check every mechanism once, then mostly explore with a little digging, and stop digging once it only re-finds what it found) into Gen3's 'what to test next' step, with the balance set by the search's own count of repeat finds, and measure it at no cost on recorded Gen3 missions.
claims_boundary: Scripted test targets except P7 (one IBM hardware run) and the reads of recorded Gen3 outcomes. No real target was contacted. No quantum advantage. Nothing here is a Model 1 result.
